# {name}

> {name} lets two businesses that do not know each other trust each other before they meet, wherever being seen
> costs something and a lot is at stake. It works in three steps: a check of each side, a private match, and an
> introduction only when both say yes.

This file is a plain-text summary of the public site for language models. It makes no claim beyond the pages it links
to, and every sentence is true on the day of the site's status check (see Status). The full text of every English page
is in [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt). The site is in English at the root and in German, Spanish, Italian and French
under /de, /es, /it and /fr, with the same pages in every language.

## The three steps

1. Check: each side confirms its email address through a link sent to it; nothing is stored before it confirms. A
   space can require gates, such as a KYC and sanctions check, recorded by a named operator. Checks of a company by
   {name} itself are planned, not built.
2. Private match: {name} compares a need and an offer criterion by criterion and gives a verdict per criterion, never
   a score. Each side sees a board card without names: neither sees the other's name or contact.
3. Both say yes: a named person at the platform approves the possible fit, then each side answers on its own. Only
   when both say yes do names and email addresses go out, directly or through the platform's team. A no on either side
   reveals nothing to the other.

## Where it stands

- The first space is for B2B trade in industrial minerals. It runs as a test instance with synthetic data; no real
  person and no real organisation uses it yet.
- A platform embeds {name} in its own pages: one script and one element, one space per market.
- Nothing of {name} is published as open source yet. Planned: the widget, the SDK, a command-line tool and the
  protocol description as open source; the checks, the checked history, the matching and the billing as a service
  {name} hosts.

## Terms

{name}, space, check, private match, board card without names, both say yes, introduction, checked history: each has
one definition, the same on the site, in the widget and in the docs. They are listed at [FAQ](/faq#terms).

## Pages

- [Home](/): the headline and a demo of the three steps with two fictional businesses, in the browser only.
- [FAQ](/faq): what {name} is, the problem it solves, how "both say yes" works, what it checks today, what is open
  source and what is hosted, who it is for, and the terms.
- [How it works](/how-it-works): a space and its market vocabulary, the ways to describe a need or an offer,
  confirming, matching with a verdict per criterion, approval and gates, both sides' yes, the introduction, who sees
  what at each stage.
- [Who sees what](/who-sees-what): one synthetic offer, stage by stage.
- [For platforms](/for-platforms) and [Integrations](/platforms): the embed, keys and origins, the console, the SDK
  and webhooks, recipes for plain HTML, Astro, Next.js and WordPress.
- [Developers](/developers): the shortest embed, an SDK example, and what is not available yet.
- [Developer docs](/developers/docs), in English: the quickstart in 5 minutes, the widget, the SDK, the CLI (planned),
  the protocol, the API reference, and what is open and what is hosted. Not published yet: the repository is private.
- [For verticals](/verticals): what a market vocabulary holds; the first space, industrial minerals.
- [Status](/status): dated, which parts run on the synthetic test space, which are built or in the contract, which
  are planned.
- [Privacy notice](/privacy), [Imprint](/imprint) and [Contact](/contact): in preparation.
